title: fastpath: gate precision toggles and strengthen fallback for KV-cache / continuous-batching
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: The fastpath execution path in the serving runtime introduced a set of precision toggles (fp16/amp/quantized kernels) and an aggressive KV-cache+continuous-batching heuristic to maximize throughput. In the field we observed rare correctness regressions and latency spikes when the fastpath engaged on boundary cases (odd sequence lengths, mixed-precision rolling, and partial KV cache hits). This PR introduces conservative gating of the fastpath via a new "safe-mode" check and a hardened fallback path to ensure correctness without sacrificing steady-state throughput.

What this does (summary):
- Adds a runtime gate that prevents fastpath precision toggles from enabling when sequence-length/skew metrics indicate high variance (safe-mode).
- Introduces an explicit fastpath->fallback handoff that preserves KV-cache invariants: on precision/kv mismatch we now materialize a small re-encoded prefix to guarantee deterministic KV state before continuing with fallback kernels.
- Strengthens the continuous-batching scheduler: the batcher now tracks per-request precision and kv-consistency tags and will split/flush batches to avoid mixing incompatible requests.
- Adds an opt-in runtime flag (runtime.fastpath.safe_mode=auto|on|off) that defaults to "auto". Auto uses real-time metrics to gate.
- Adds runtime telemetry and a rollout plan to monitor correctness and perf regressions.

Motivation: We want the fastpath performance benefits in the common case but cannot accept occasional correctness regressions or large latency outliers. Prior fixes toggled precision globally which reduced throughput. This change keeps fastpath available but makes it conservative at the per-request level and provides a deterministic fallback that is cheap to take.

Design notes:
- Safe-mode gating: compute a rolling variance on recent sequence lengths and KV-hit ratios at the shard level. If variance > threshold -> mark upcoming requests as safe-mode candidates and disallow precision downcasting for them.
- Hand-off: when a request enters fallback due to precision mismatch or KV inconsistency, we materialize at most N tokens (configurable, default 8) using a deterministic encoder to rebuild the KV state, then continue on the fallback kernel. This is O(prefix) work and avoids full re-evaluation.
- Scheduler: continuous batch builder groups requests by (precision_tag, kv_consistency_tag). When mixing would reduce correctness we split batch boundaries earlier; when it hurts throughput we fall back to a small-buffered greedy flush.

Files changed (high level):
- src/runtime/fastpath.rs: adds gating logic and safe-mode flag parsing.
- src/runtime/fallback.rs: implements materialize_prefix_for_fallback() and KV invariant checks.
- src/runtime/kv_cache.rs: KV state tagging and deterministic re-encode helper.
- src/runtime/scheduler.rs: batch tag bookkeeping and split heuristics.
- runtime/config/defaults.toml: new fastpath.safe_mode config.
- tests/kv_cache_tests.rs: new regression tests for mixed-precision KV handoffs.
- perf/bench/continuous_batching.yml: perf harness updates.
- docs/fastpath.md: design and rollout notes.
- ci/workflows/runtime-tests.yml: adds a focused scenario to guard regressions.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for the new deterministic re-encoder and KV-tag invariants (added).
- SST: synthetic workload that mixes long/short sequences with varying precision; baseline vs new behavior shows no correctness diffs across 100k generated requests.
- Perf: microbenchmarks show fastpath throughput unchanged for stable workloads; tail latency (95/99) reduced compared to prior ad-hoc fixes. See numbers below.

Perf numbers (avg of 5 runs, n1-standard-GPU):
- Stable homogeneous workload (fp16, long seqs): baseline fastpath: 100k tok/s, this PR: 99.5k tok/s (-0.5%).
- Mixed variance workload: baseline (no safe gating): 60k tok/s with 99p latency spikes; this PR: 78k tok/s with stable 99p latency and zero correctness diffs.
- Continuous batching overhead (scheduler split cases): median throughput drop in split-heavy workloads ~6% vs previous global disable which dropped ~30%.

Checklist:
- [x] Add safe-mode config and gate code.
- [x] Implement deterministic prefix materialization for fallback.
- [x] Scheduler tagging and split flush heuristics.
- [x] Unit + integration tests.
- [x] Perf harness updates and benchmarks.
- [x] Docs + rollout notes.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary: enable safe_mode=auto for 10% of traffic, monitor new telemetry (kv_handoffs, safe_mode_engagement, fastpath_fallbacks, correctness_regressions).
2) If stable for 48h -> 50% rollout and run full e2e tests.
3) 100% rollout and continue monitoring.

Backwards compatibility: Default is "auto" to preserve existing behavior unless metrics indicate risk. The explicit on/off flag supports quick rollback.

Notes: The approach favors deterministic correctness at the expense of very small prefix work during handoffs. This preserves the fastpath benefits for the common case while eliminating the rare but costly correctness incidents previously observed.

review_comments: Jonah Kim: Should the safe_mode threshold be per-shard or global? I'd prefer per-shard due to hardware skews.
Aisha Patel: Agreed, implemented per-shard rolling variance. Kept a global override in config for emergency ops.
Miguel Torres: The deterministic materialize step looks good but we should cap the prefix length. What is the failure mode if encoder changes?
Aisha Patel: Capped to 8 tokens by default and added schema-guarded encoder version check; if encoder version mismatches we force a full fallback and emit a metric.
Ethan Zhang: CI initially failed on e2e-batching due to a flakiness in the harness. After increasing the harness timeout and locking RNG seeds, tests are green.
Jonah Kim: Approving pending a small docs addition showing how to flip the runtime flag during rollback.
Aisha Patel: Added docs note and rollout checklist. Ready to merge.
ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (stable workloads ~-0.5% throughput, mixed workloads +30% effective)
release_notes: Conservative fastpath gating and deterministic KV-cache fallback to eliminate rare correctness regressions while preserving throughput for stable workloads. Adds runtime.fastpath.safe_mode config and telemetry to monitor fallbacks.
notes_for_ops: Enable runtime.fastpath.safe_mode=auto in canary initially (10%). Monitor metrics: fastpath_safe_mode_engagement, fastpath_fallbacks_per_minute, kv_handoff_errors. Ops can force runtime.fastpath.safe_mode=off to disable gating, or =on to be conservative.
